sourceBindings.text: Point to site-specific exit, eye-wash, shower, fire extinguisher and waste containers; show relevant SDS and choose compatible PPE before touching the sample.
Trainer records each learner's demonstration and any correction.
Read source label against field record and record the full sample ID, collection date, location/depth and collector.
Trainer signs identity match.
Confirm the requested analysis. If this protocol calls for drying, spread a thin labelled layer in a clean ventilated place away from direct sun; log start, observation and actual completion time.
Trainer observes the learner's preparation and completion across stages; pre-dried sample cannot earn this evidence.
Gently break dry aggregates without grinding stones; pass through the required 2 mm sieve and retain the correct identified fine-earth fraction.
Trainer observes tool choice, cleaning and material separation.
Weigh and seal the assessment-card 450–550 g final product, check the complete matching label and explain a test for which drying would be inappropriate.
Trainer checks all product criteria and records actual learner performance.

units.delivery: Explain calmly and naturally to agricultural vocational learners in clear English. Read only the supplied connected passage with natural pauses. Preserve all negations, conditions, scene-safety restrictions and limits of training. Do not add medical advice, diagnoses, character voices, an introduction, music or an extra summary.

sourceBindings.text: Trainer observes the learner identify the eye-wash, shower, exit, extinguisher and designated waste route; use the applicable label/SDS; select task- and chemical-compatible PPE; match beaker, graduated cylinder, sieve, mortar/pestle, balance, pH device and colorimeter to their intended roles.

Pass only with individual, safe demonstration and recorded trainer evidence. A quiz, group action or photograph of equipment is insufficient; unsafe actions pause the practice and require remediation.

Trainer records sample ID at receipt, pre-drying condition, method requested, learner's own drying start/end or other protocol-specific handling, clean thin-layer tray away from sun/contamination, gentle aggregate breakdown, 2 mm sieve use where appropriate and retained sample identity.

Pass only when the learner personally performs every required stage over actual elapsed time and the trainer records it. A pre-dried supplied sample permits crush/sieve assessment only and cannot prove drying skill.

Trainer checks no visible stones/roots/leaves, appropriately dry crumbly sample for this assessment task, uniform sieved material, measured 450–550 g, securely sealed bag, accurate date, Field ID, sample depth and collector's name matching the full field record, plus the learner's explanation of method exceptions.

Pass only if all product criteria and individual process evidence are present; the 450–550 g tolerance belongs to this assessment card, not every laboratory. A correct final bag does not prove who dried it.

sourceBindings.text: This nine-action observation card spans sample preparation and the later pH step. The actions assessed here are PPE, gentle aggregate breakup and 2 mm sieving. The supplied sample is already air-dried, so this activity does not demonstrate your drying skill. The card’s 20 g / 20 mL / 1 minute / 15 minutes and calibrated stable reading belong to the later pH teaching scenario and remain subject to its protocol.

Trainer checks six product criteria: no visible debris; appropriately air-dried crumbly condition; gently crushed and sieved uniform texture; 450–550 g; secure seal; legible matching date, Field ID, depth and collector name. Observe individual drying and preparation separately so the product is not mistaken for process proof.
